Position Description:

The People Business Partner partners with ServiceTrade leaders to help them lead stronger teams and make better people decisions.

Reporting to the Director, Talent - This role focuses on manager enablement, performance, talent development, organizational effectiveness, and employee relations, while helping improve the People programs and processes that support the business.

Just as important, this is the person who makes ServiceTrade's People Manager Success Factors real for the leaders they support — coaching managers to assess and recognize great talent, manage people risk before it becomes a crisis, translate strategy into work their teams actually understand, keep raising the bar instead of settling, and execute through their people instead of around them. It's how our managers lead in practice, not just in a training deck — and it's what keeps values like Customer Obsessed, Resilient, and Evolving (yes, even a little Weird) alive day to day, not just on a wall.

We're looking for someone who works independently, asks good questions, uses sound judgment, and brings thoughtful recommendations to leaders.

Why ServiceTrade:

You’ll belong here from the start.

We bring together kind, curious people with diverse perspectives and trust them with meaningful work. You’ll have ownership, clarity, and support to solve real problems, make a visible impact for our customers, and continue growing as your role evolves.

About You:

You build strong relationships with leaders and are someone they involve early when working through a people or organizational decision.
You are comfortable working through ambiguity and figuring out what is really driving an issue.
You know when an established process is helpful and when the situation calls for a more tailored approach.
You bring a point of view and recommendation, while staying open to additional context.
You balance empathy with clear expectations and accountability.
You can recognize when a challenge is organizational or structural rather than purely a People issue.
You handle sensitive information with care and communicate directly.
You use AI thoughtfully to make preparation, analysis, and administrative work more efficient while keeping human judgment at the center.

Key Responsibilities and Activities:

Talent Management, Performance & Succession

Lead Talent Review and calibration discussions and help leaders make thoughtful, consistent talent decisions.
Support promotion decisions and identify broader patterns in performance and talent data.
Partner with leaders on succession planning and retention risk.
Help turn Talent Review outcomes into development, performance, succession, and staffing actions.

Learning & Development

Partner with leaders to identify development needs across their teams
Help translate performance, Talent Reviews, and succession insights into practical development actions
Support manager development programs and leadership learning initiatives
Facilitate or co-facilitate manager sessions, workshops, and team development conversations
Recommend development approaches that are practical, relevant to the business, and easy for managers to apply

People Data & Insights

Use engagement, performance, retention, and workforce data to help leaders understand what is happening in their organizations.
Identify patterns and questions worth exploring and bring recommendations when appropriate.
Use data as a starting point for discussion while incorporating business context before drawing conclusions.

Program & Process Ownership

Own assigned People programs and processes end to end, including execution, measurement, and improvement.
Look for opportunities to simplify and improve how work gets done.
Keep documentation current and ensure ownership is clear.

AI-Enabled Ways of Working

Use AI to improve preparation, synthesis, analysis, and documentation where appropriate.
Look for repeatable ways AI can make People workflows more efficient and effective.
Apply sound judgment to AI outputs and ensure employment decisions remain human-led.

Knowledge and Skills:

3-7 years of progressive human resources / business partner experience, including direct ownership of employee relations, performance management, and organizational design.
Proven experience partnering directly with leaders (Director level and below) on people and organizational issues preferably in a SaaS or high-growth technology company
Strong employee relations and performance management judgment, including experience handling complex or sensitive situations independently.
Solid working knowledge of employment law.
Experience supporting or facilitating manager and leadership development, including translating business or talent needs into practical learning experiences.
Experience with Talent Review, calibration, succession planning, or other talent-management processes.
Comfortable using people data to identify patterns, ask better questions, and support leader decisions.
Experience owning People programs or processes from planning through creativity, execution and improvement.
Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to navigate difficult conversations clearly and thoughtfully.
Comfortable working in ambiguity and bringing a recommendation rather than waiting for direction.
Willingness and ability to use AI as part of day-to-day work to improve preparation, analysis, documentation, and efficiency.
Comfortable working across a modern SaaS tech stack, including tools such as Slack, Notion, and Lattice.

A few things you’ll want to know:

What does ServiceTrade do?

ServiceTrade is a best-in-class field service management platform that helps commercial fire protection and mechanical service contractors build efficient and growing businesses. With more than a decade of innovation and 1500 customers, ServiceTrade streamlines operations from the field to the office, boosts technician productivity, and enhances the end-customer experience.

Ok, so why should I care about that?

Our customers do essential work — often behind the scenes — and our software helps them do it better. They’re smart, hardworking people, and we take pride in helping them grow their businesses, earn more revenue, employ more skilled workers, and deliver greater value to their own customers. When you work at ServiceTrade, your impact extends beyond our walls, supporting communities and markets you might never have thought about — and making work that truly matters every day.

What kind of working environment do you have?

We’re a growing business focused on building with intention and operating with purpose. You’ll have meaningful responsibility and the trust to do your best work from the start. We encourage calculated risks and bold experimentation, while providing opportunities to learn, grow, and turn today’s lessons into tomorrow’s breakthroughs—all in service of big ambitions and real customer impact.

Learn more about our culture and values on our About Us page.

Flexible Spending Account and Dependant Care Account

Go ahead and apply! Let’s get to know each other.

The People Operations Manager is a core owner of Gold Leaf’s People function, responsible for managing day-to-day people processes with accuracy and care. The role partners directly with managers across the full employee lifecycle and improves the systems and structures that allow GLF to attract, develop, and retain the Right People in the Right Seats. Core responsibilities of the People Operations Manager include:

Centralized People Operations (75% of time)

The People Operations Manager owns the execution, improvement, and communication of GLF's centralized people processes, serving as a trusted, day-to-day point of contact for all employees. This role challenges the status quo to continuously refine people processes, strengthen cultural alignment, and enhance employee experience.
Own execution of centralized processes: hiring, onboarding, payroll, benefits, performance management, safety, employee experience, and HR compliance
Identify process gaps and implement low-bureaucracy improvements through automation, elimination, or outsourcing
Build self-service resources that let employees navigate the People function independently
Serve as a responsive, knowledgeable resource for employees, providing clear support and building their confidence navigating the employee experience at GLF
Own Rippling as the single source of truth for people data, ensuring accuracy and building automations that reduce manual work
Partner with internal teams to ensure they have the access and information they need from People systems to do their jobs
Support the co-employment complexity of GLF's FLC model, including seasonal transitions and I-9 compliance at scale, so hourly farm workers experience Gold Leaf's culture even through contractor relationships

HR Business Partner (25% of time)

The People Operations Manager partners directly with managers as a hands-on people expert, providing credible, culturally grounded guidance across the employee lifecycle.
Own the RPRS (Right Person Right Seat) process end to end, coaching managers through evaluation conversations that drive real personnel decisions
Partner with managers on hiring, onboarding, performance management, and employee relations with sound judgment and low bureaucracy
Provide guidance that reflects GLF's culture and operating principles, equipping managers with the tools, frameworks, and knowledge to handle people situations with greater confidence over time
Contribute to GLF's talent strategy by identifying patterns, gaps, and opportunities surfaced through day-to-day people operations
Partner with the VP of Operations on culture programming: quarterly gatherings, recognition programs, and the structures that make Gold Leaf's culture durable across a decentralized team
Support the delivery of a differentiated, best-in-class employee experience rooted in GLF's culture, operating principles, and long-term vision

Suggested Skills And Experience

jobs.title: People Operations Manager, Data & Reporting
jobs.description:
Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why this role?

We're hiring a People Operations Manager to own our People data and the reporting built on top of it, alongside a slice of the operational work that generates it.

Cohere is scaling fast and leadership needs numbers they can trust. Today those numbers take too long to produce and they don't always agree with each other. Reporting is only as good as the data underneath it, which is why this role runs real processes as well as reporting on them.

This is a hands-on building role. You will own headcount, attrition and cost reporting, define what our metrics actually mean, and own benefits administration and employee records end to end. You will own the answer, not just the spreadsheet. A useful lens; this role means nobody has to debate whose number is right.

You'll join a small HR Operations team during our Rippling implementation, which means greenfield opportunity and real influence over how our data is structured for the next few years.

What You'll Do

Own the numbers

Own headcount, attrition and people cost reporting end to end
Build the exec and board level reporting our leadership relies on
Define what our metrics mean, rather than producing whatever is asked for

Fix the data underneath

Reconcile People and Finance headcount, and keep them reconciled
Clean up the taxonomies that make reporting unreliable, starting with termination reasons
Chase the data quality problems nobody has asked you to chase
Build the checks that stop bad data entering in the first place

Own the data model

Own our employee data model, definitions and governance
Work with the HRIS team so the system supports the reporting we need
Push and challenge current systems to meet your data vision

Own Benefits Administration And Records

Own US and global benefits administration, renewal cycles and open enrolment
Own employee records, employment verification and data requests
Support the front line team who handle day to day employee questions

Make reporting self-serve

Automate the recurring reporting so it produces itself
Give managers and leaders access to their own numbers
Reduce the number of requests that need a person at all

Build For What's Coming

Produce reporting that stands up to audit and external diligence
Work with Finance and IT on the controls and evidence our data needs to carry
Design for a company several times our current size

Manage a team

Led and developed a high-performing team through regular coaching, feedback, and performance management while maintaining team cohesion and morale
Managed day-to-day operations and resource allocation for a small team, balancing project priorities, resolving conflicts, and ensuring timely delivery of deliverables within budget constraints

You may be a good fit if you

5+ years of people analytics and reporting experience, within fast-paced, scaling environments
Meaningful experience delivering people operations solutions across all aspects of the talent journey
Experienced in HRIS implementation or migration
Experience building reports from scratch
Proactively identify and resolve data quality issues, maintaining high standards for clean, reliable analytics data
Effectively communicate data insights by explaining numerical findings, their source methodology, and rationale for discrepancies with alternative interpretations
Write clearly and document by default
Have run operations across multiple countries and entities, including EOR or contractor populations
Are comfortable anywhere across the employee journey, from hire to exit
Pick up new tools quickly and become the person others ask
Enjoy building elegant solutions to messy operational problems

Bonus if you have

Worked in Rippling, or implemented it
People management experience
Built reporting in a BI tool, or worked comfortably in SQL
Been in a company through IPO readiness or SOC 2 and SOX preparation

What we're not looking for

Someone who waits for a report request and fills it. This role decides what we measure and makes the underlying data good enough to trust. If you would rather be handed a spec than write one, this is not the role for you.

Full-Time Employees At Cohere Enjoy These Perks

A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.
Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.
RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.
100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.
Annual enrichment benefits:

Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.

Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)
Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

How And Where We Work

Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.
For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.
For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.
Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form, and we will work together to meet your needs.

All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers page.

Spotlight is not just a place to execute campaigns—it’s a blank canvas where ambitious people can build real leverage, take on increasing responsibility, and grow into senior operators quickly. Our culture is high-performing, entrepreneurial, and unapologetically ambitious.

Join us, and you’ll have the trust, resources, and runway to redefine what’s possible for the world’s leading brands.

The Role

The HR Generalist & Talent Acquisition Specialist will serve as Spotlight Media's primary recruiter and HR point person.

The ideal candidate is someone who genuinely enjoys recruiting and interviewing, knows how to identify strong candidates, and can quickly understand what makes someone a good fit for a particular role.

You will be responsible for managing the recruiting process from sourcing through initial interviews while also overseeing the company's day-to-day HR administration, including onboarding, offboarding, payroll coordination, time-off tracking, employee documentation, and employee relations.

This person will interact with candidates, employees, managers, and leadership on a regular basis, so excellent verbal and written communication skills are essential.

Key Responsibilities

Talent Acquisition & Recruiting — Primary Responsibility

Own Spotlight Media's recruiting process from job opening through candidate handoff/hire.
Develop and execute proactive recruiting strategies to identify qualified candidates.
Conduct outbound recruiting through LinkedIn, email, direct messaging, job boards, professional networks, and other channels.
Source candidates for a variety of positions across the organization.
Review resumes and applications and determine which candidates meet the requirements of each role.
Conduct initial screening calls and first-round interviews.
Develop thoughtful interview questions and evaluation criteria for different positions.
Assess candidates based on qualifications, communication skills, experience, cultural/team fit, and potential for success in the role.
Provide clear and objective candidate feedback to hiring managers and leadership.
Coordinate interviews between candidates and hiring managers.
Maintain an organized candidate pipeline and recruiting database/ATS.
Follow up with candidates throughout the recruiting process and provide a professional candidate experience.
Help develop and continuously improve Spotlight Media's recruiting process.
Track recruiting metrics such as applicants, interviews, candidates sourced, time-to-hire, and hiring conversion rates.
Build and maintain a pipeline of potential candidates for frequently hired positions.
Help write and optimize job descriptions and job postings for LinkedIn, Indeed, and other recruiting platforms.

HR Administration

Manage the employee onboarding process for new hires.
Ensure new employees complete required documentation and onboarding requirements.
Coordinate equipment, systems access, accounts, and other onboarding needs.
Manage employee offboarding and ensure a smooth transition when employees leave the company.
Coordinate the return of company property and removal of access to company systems.
Maintain accurate and organized employee records.
Track vacation, sick time, and other employee time-off.
Maintain company HR policies and documentation.
Assist with payroll processing and ensure payroll information is accurate and submitted on time.
Coordinate with payroll providers and/or internal leadership regarding payroll issues.
Maintain accurate employee information and compensation records.
Help ensure HR processes are consistently followed across the organization.

Employee Relations & Management Support

Serve as a trusted point of contact for employees regarding HR-related questions and concerns.
Partner with managers and leadership on employee performance and workplace issues.
Help managers navigate employee performance concerns and disciplinary situations.
Participate in employee termination processes when warranted.
Conduct termination/offboarding meetings when appropriate and ensure the process is handled professionally and respectfully.
Maintain appropriate confidentiality when dealing with sensitive employee information.
Help leadership identify and address employee-related issues before they become larger problems.

Required Qualifications

What We're Looking For

3+ years of professional HR and/or recruiting experience.
Significant hands-on recruiting experience, particularly with outbound candidate sourcing.
Demonstrated experience conducting phone/video screening interviews and first-round interviews.
Experience recruiting for multiple types of roles, rather than specializing in only one position or industry.
Strong understanding of the full recruiting lifecycle.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Extremely articulate and comfortable communicating with candidates and employees.
Strong interviewing and candidate-evaluation skills.
Highly organized and able to manage multiple open positions and HR responsibilities simultaneously.
Strong attention to detail.
Comfortable handling confidential and sensitive employee information.
Experience with HRIS, ATS, Ashby, payroll, recruiting, or other HR technology platforms.
Strong proficiency with Google Workspace and common business software.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in a fast-growing company or startup environment.
Experience recruiting for remote or distributed teams.
Experience recruiting for sales, marketing, account management, operations, or other professional positions.
Experience in digital marketing, e-commerce, creator economy, social media, or TikTok Shop.
Experience developing recruiting processes from the ground up.
Experience working with employees across multiple geographic locations.
Experience with payroll administration and employee benefits administration.

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is first and foremost a great recruiter and interviewer
.

You should be someone who can look at a job description, understand what success in the position looks like, identify where strong candidates are likely to be found, reach out to them, and determine during an initial conversation whether they are worth moving forward.

You should also be comfortable switching gears. One day you may be sourcing candidates for an Account Manager; the next you may be onboarding a new employee, helping a manager address a performance issue, processing payroll information, or conducting an employee offboarding.

We Are Looking For Someone Who

Is confident and highly articulate.
Can build rapport quickly with candidates.
Knows how to ask good questions and, more importantly, listen to the answers.
Can distinguish between someone who interviews well and someone who is actually qualified.
Is comfortable conducting difficult conversations when necessary.
Takes ownership rather than waiting to be told what to do.
Is highly organized and follows through.
Can handle confidential information with discretion.
Is comfortable working in a fast-paced, growing company.
Is comfortable recruiting for positions they may not have personally held.
Has excellent judgment when evaluating people.
Is professional but approachable.
Can balance the needs of employees, managers, and the company.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role will primarily be measured by the quality and effectiveness of our recruiting process.

Within This Role, You Will Be Expected To

Consistently build strong candidate pipelines for our open positions.
Generate qualified candidates through proactive outbound recruiting.
Conduct high-quality screening and first-round interviews.
Help hiring managers spend their time interviewing only the most promising candidates.
Improve our overall time-to-hire without sacrificing candidate quality.
Create a professional and positive candidate experience.
Keep our HR processes organized, accurate, and compliant.
Ensure employees have a smooth experience when joining and leaving Spotlight Media.
Provide leadership with reliable HR information and support.
Become a trusted resource for both employees and management.

Why Join Spotlight Media?

Spotlight Media is a growing company operating in one of the most rapidly evolving areas of digital commerce.

This is an opportunity to join at a stage where you can have a meaningful impact on how the company builds its team and develops its HR infrastructure
.

You will have significant ownership over recruiting and the opportunity to help build the processes, systems, and standards that will support Spotlight Media as we continue to grow.

If you are an experienced recruiter who also has strong HR generalist capabilities—and you enjoy building teams, interviewing people, and helping a growing company hire great talent—we would love to hear from you.

Compensation & Benefits

Competitive salary based on experience
Medical, Dental and Vision
401K
Take it as you need it PTO after 90 days.
Remote work environment
This role reports to the GM of Spotlight Media
Opportunity for professional growth within a rapidly growing company

Spotlight Media is an equal opportunity employer.

Compensation Range: $50K - $65.5K

Owner of full-cycle recruitment: Manage requisition intake, job posting, candidate sourcing, screening, coordinating interviews, offer management, and onboarding handoffs for roles across functions and geographies.

Assessment and selection: Conduct structured interviews, competency assessments, and reference checks; ensure selection decisions align with company values and hiring best practices.
Hiring operations: Maintain accurate candidate and requisition data in the applicant tracking system (ATS); manage offer approvals, background checks, and onboarding documentation.
Diversity, equity, and inclusion: Drive inclusive sourcing practices and support initiatives to increase diverse representation across the workforce.
Recruiting metrics and continuous improvement: Track KPIs such as time-to-fill, quality of hire, and sourcing channel effectiveness; analyze data and recommend process improvements.
Employer branding & recruitment marketing: Support local and global employer branding efforts, attend recruitment events, and develop content to attract top talent.
Compliance and confidentiality: Ensure recruitment practices comply with local employment laws and internal policies; handle confidential information with discretion.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business, Psychology, or a related field preferred.
3+ years of full-cycle recruitment experience, ideally with exposure to international or multi-region hiring.
Experience using an applicant tracking system (ATS) and recruitment tools; comfortable maintaining accurate data and producing recruitment reports.
Strong sourcer skills with proven ability to find and engage passive candidates across channels.
Excellent interpersonal, communication, and negotiation skills; able to build credibility with stakeholders at all levels.
Cultural sensitivity and experience working with diverse teams across time zones.
Analytical mindset with experience tracking recruiting metrics and using data to drive decisions.
High level of organization, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple requisitions simultaneously.
Familiarity with local employment laws and hiring compliance in multiple jurisdictions preferred.
Willingness to work flexible hours occasionally to accommodate different time zones.

Competitive compensation and benefits, including health coverage and performance-based rewards.
Opportunities for professional growth through training programs and a supportive learning culture.
Collaborative global team and a chance to shape hiring strategies across markets.
A commitment to work-life balance with flexible work arrangements where applicable.

jobs.title: Associate People Operations Business Partner
jobs.description:
Knix is an award-winning intimate apparel and activewear brand that is re-inventing intimates for real life. Through our innovative products and our engaged community, we are empowering people everywhere to be unapologetically free. Launched in 2013, we are one of the fastest-growing intimate apparel brands in North America and are globally recognized as an innovator within the apparel space. We reach over 3 million customers through our online stores, Knix retail locations across North America and channels such as wholesale and Amazon. We are revolutionizing the apparel industry with our best-in-class customer experience, innovative products and brands Knix, Kt by Knix, and Mntd. Come join us if you are looking for a purpose-driven and authentic career!

We’re looking for an Associate HR Business Partner who will support Western Canada and is energized by supporting high-performing, people-first retail teams. In this role, you will work closely with District Managers, store leaders and hourly team members to support day-to-day HR needs while helping scale initiatives that keep pace with a fast-moving retail environment.

You will support the full employee lifecycle across our stores by delivering HR programs, coaching leaders, addressing employee concerns, supporting onboarding and development, and ensuring a consistent and positive experience for our retail teams. Key focus areas include performance and coaching, employee relations, staffing and workforce planning, HR program deployment, retail compliance and employee engagement.

As a core member of the People Team, you will partner with Retail Operations, People Operations, and Talent Acquisition to drive business goals while ensuring our retail employees feel supported, empowered, and set up for success every day.

About You:

You are a hands-on, approachable HR professional with a people-first mindset and a passion for supporting hourly retail employees and leaders.
You build trust quickly and collaborate effectively with store leaders, retail associates, and cross-functional teams.
You thrive in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment and can shift priorities based on business needs.
You enjoy working on the ground—with stores, with leaders, and with associates—to understand challenges and create practical, scalable solutions.
You are proactive and resourceful, with strong coaching and listening skills that help leaders develop their teams and navigate employee situations confidently.
You are excited about building repeatable processes, tools, and resources as our retail network expands.
You bring strong judgment, discretion, and a collaborative approach to problem solving.

The Opportunity:

Serve as the primary People partner for assigned retail stores, building trusted relationships with District Managers, store leaders, and team members.
Coach and support retail leaders across performance management, delivering feedback, communication skills, employee development, team dynamics, and day to day people decisions.
Support employee relations matters including conflict resolution, policy interpretation, performance concerns, and workplace issues, escalating more complex or higher risk matters when appropriate.
Support investigations and maintain clear and appropriate documentation.
Help ensure employment practices across assigned stores comply with applicable legislation and align with Knix policies and practices.
Partner with Retail leaders on retention, development, and talent movement across the retail network.
Partner with Talent Acquisition and Retail Operations to support hiring, onboarding, and integration of retail team members.
Deliver People, learning, performance, engagement, feedback, and recognition programs across stores, helping ensure they are practical and accessible for our retail teams.
Gather feedback from stores and bring forward themes, opportunities, and recommendations that can strengthen People programs and the broader retail employee experience.
Use workforce data, employee feedback, and store trends to identify patterns and opportunities across areas such as turnover, retention, attendance, engagement, and staffing.
Partner with fellow Business Partners and the broader People Team to create consistency across stores while recognizing the unique needs of different teams and markets.
Support organizational changes and People initiatives by helping leaders communicate effectively and navigate their teams through change.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s Degree in Human Resources, Business, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. CHRP/CHRL designation (or in progress) is an asset.
Minimum of 3 years of HR experience, with at least 1–2 years supporting retail or hourly employee groups.
Strong understanding of employment legislation in Canada (multi-jurisdiction experience is an asset).
Experience supporting employee relations, store-level coaching, onboarding, performance conversations, and HR program delivery.
Proven ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and maintain confidentiality.
Comfortable working in a fast-paced retail environment with agility, resilience, and a continuous improvement mindset.
Solid foundational knowledge of HR practices including performance management, employee relations, engagement, workforce planning, and change management.

Salary:

Annual salary starting at $80,000.00

Compensation & Care

Transparency is at the heart of everything we do, including how we pay. The posted expected hourly rate for this role represents candidates developing new skills within the position. Increased rates represent those who are more proficient or have achieved mastery and deep institutional knowledge over time.

Rewards are not just about your regular pay and monthly bonuses. We believe rewards should support your whole life, not just your shift. That’s why for permanent full-time employees
, we cover 100% of the premiums for extended health and dental plans from your first day. You’ll also gain access to mental health support through our Employee Assistance Programs through our partners at Dialogue who provide virtual coaching, therapy, and counseling.

When your family grows, we’re there for you. Our Paid Parental Leave plan tops up salary to 80%
for eligible permanent, full-time employees. We also invest in your future with a RRSP matching program
for permanent full-time team members. Plus, you’ll enjoy a 50% discount
on Knix products because we want you to love what you sell.

We want to share that we may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to help us screen and assess applications. While technology helps us stay organized, every hiring decision at Knix is made by real people who care about finding the best addition to our team. We use these tools to support our process, not to replace the human connection that makes our culture special.

How We Hire

Our people are what make Knix, Knix! Our people are passionate and have a strong belief in our mission. Our people are naturally curious and ambitious by nature. Employees feel respected and supported at Knix. We take an inclusive and equitable approach offering the same interview experience to every candidate we meet with. Knix is an equal opportunity employer, we celebrate everyone and their intersecting identities. We know and believe that diverse and inclusive teams empower us to make better decisions and inspire innovation so that we can better serve our customers and community. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations and will work with you to meet your needs. If you are a person with a disability and require assistance during the application process, please don’t hesitate to reach out! We celebrate our inclusive work environment and welcome members of all backgrounds and perspectives to apply.

jobs.title: People Operations Lead
jobs.description:
About Edra

Edra is solving one of the hardest problems in enterprise AI: AI models are generic but company processes are specific. We build AI agents that learn how processes actually run, and then run their operations.

We're a Series A startup, backed by Sequoia and other leading VC firms, led by Co-Founders who created and led Forward Deployed AI Engineering at Palantir, and we're growing our team in New York and London. We're a deeply technical team of engineers, AI researchers, and strategists with a high bar for talent and a shared belief that exceptional people are the foundation of everything great we'll build.

The Role

Edra is 30+ people across New York and London, with aggressive hiring plans in both offices. Every one of those people runs through an offer, payroll in one of two countries, equity in one of two tax regimes, benefits, and the compliance layer underneath it all. We've laid the foundation; now we want someone to own it, and to build the version that gets us to 60, 100, and beyond.

You'll own the employee lifecycle end to end in both countries: US and UK payroll, benefits in both regimes, onboarding, and people compliance across two jurisdictions. At most companies, people ops is carved into slices; here you own the whole stack, with real autonomy to determine how it runs. You'll own these systems internally, working directly with our payroll providers, benefits brokers, accountants, and employment counsel where specialist expertise is needed.

That's the exciting part, so we'll be specific about it: this is a builder and operator role. You'll inherit working processes and be expected to replace each one as we outgrow it: automating what's manual, rebuilding for scale, and designing the systems a much larger Edra will still be running down the line. And because we're an AI company, we expect you to build like one. Edra's platform is available to you as a tool for your own function, and we want you using it (along with everything else in a modern AI startup stack) to build and run a people operation that's leaner, faster, and more precise than a traditional people operation. If you've ever looked at a payroll reconciliation or an onboarding checklist and thought “a system should be doing this!” this is the place to prove it.

One thing to be upfront about: comp philosophy, equity strategy, and performance management remain Founder-owned. You'll make those programs operationally excellent: the data, tooling, process, communication, and execution behind them.

What You'll Do

Be the first point of contact for operational people questions (payroll, benefits, leave, equity administration, and employment logistics) and resolve them quickly and clearly.
Own US and UK payroll end to end: run it, reconcile it, handle joiners and leavers, catch problems before they reach a paycheck, and fix the ones that do fast.
Design and build our onboarding program from first principles, so new hires are set up to take ownership and have impact from day one, in either office.
Automate onboarding and offboarding processes across both entities: equipment and access provisioning, benefits enrollment, compliance training, and more.
Administer benefits in both countries: US healthcare and 401(k), including open enrollment and renewals; UK pension and benefits.
Own the operational compliance calendar across both countries, including required payroll, benefits, employment, and personnel processes and filings.
Keep Rippling accurate as the source of record for headcount, comp, and org data, and extend it wherever it can take work off a human
Build automations and internal tooling for repetitive people workflows, using Edra’s own platform and other AI tools wherever they can improve speed, accuracy, or employee experience.

What We’re Looking For

You've owned significant parts of people operations at a startup through a growth phase. You've personally processed payroll, fixed benefits enrollment errors, and onboarded new team members, not just managed vendors who did.
You've worked across US and UK employment infrastructure, or have international people ops experience and can close the gap quickly.
You default to systems. When something breaks twice, you fix the process, and when a task is repetitive, you automate it rather than staffing it.
You're curious about what AI tooling can do for an operations function, and you'd rather experiment and find out than wait for a vendor to tell you.
You're detail-oriented at the level this work requires. Errors in payroll and benefits are visible to everyone—you make sure they don’t happen.
You write clearly, especially when explaining equity, benefits, and policy to people who aren't specialists.
You handle confidential comp and performance information with discretion.

Bonus Points

UK payroll and pensions depth
Experience standing up new benefits programs in the US and UK
Fluency with Rippling
Track record of building automation or tooling inside an ops function

Watch our Series A announcement video
Read our blog post from our launch

Private medical & dental coverage in the UK

Galaxy Digital Inc. (Nasdaq: GLXY) is a global leader in digital assets and data center infrastructure, growing the economy that runs on code. What We Value

We are a diverse team of free thinkers, and fast movers united to help investors and creators energize the global economy. We are looking for individuals who thrive in a culture of builders and overachievers and embrace high performance, transparent feedback, and a mission-first approach. Our culture shapes our way of working and gets us where we want to be.

Seek Excellence.

Who You Are

Galaxy is seeking a People Operations Manager, Global Payroll & HRIS to join our People team in a hands-on, execution-focused role supporting our global workforce. This position will initially join on a temporary-to-permanent basis and will play a critical role in two key areas: global payroll operations and the implementation of Workday, with a targeted go-live date of January 1, 2027. In your first three-six months, success will mean helping Galaxy deliver a clean and well-controlled Workday go-live, ensuring payroll readiness and data integrity, and establishing scalable processes that can transition into steady-state People Operations

Leading up to go-live, this individual will partner closely with People, Payroll, Finance, Technology, external implementation partners, and other key stakeholders to support the successful implementation of Workday. This will include data validation and migration, business process design, testing, integrations, payroll readiness, documentation, and change management.

At the same time, this person will help manage and strengthen Galaxy's global payroll operations, ensuring employees are paid accurately and on time and that payroll processes, controls, data, and vendor relationships can scale with the organization.

Following implementation, the role will transition toward ongoing ownership and optimization of Workday and global payroll operations, including system administration, data integrity, reporting, process improvement, controls, and the employee experience.

We're looking for someone who enjoys being close to the details while understanding the broader operational picture - someone who can identify an issue in a payroll reconciliation or employee record, work cross-functionally to resolve it, and then improve the underlying process so it doesn't happen again.

What You’ll Do

Workday Implementation & HRIS

Global Payroll

Review payroll inputs and outputs to ensure employees are paid accurately, completely, and on time.
Perform payroll audits, reconciliations, and variance analyses and proactively investigate and resolve discrepancies.
Coordinate employee lifecycle changes impacting payroll, including new hires, terminations, compensation changes, bonuses, benefits deductions, leaves, and other employee changes.
Partner with Finance on payroll funding, reconciliations, reporting, and related accounting requirements.

Manage day-to-day relationships with payroll vendors, escalating and resolving issues while holding partners accountable for service and accuracy.
Maintain payroll calendars, controls, documentation, and standard operating procedures.
Identify opportunities to standardize and strengthen global payroll processes as Galaxy continues to grow.

People Operations

Support employee inquiries related to payroll, HR systems, and People processes, providing a high level of service and discretion.

Help document processes and maintain SOPs for HRIS, payroll, and people operations workflows.
Respond to employee and manager inquiries related to payroll, HR data, and system access with a high level of accuracy and discretion.

What We’re Looking For

6+ years of relevant experience in People Operations, payroll, HRIS, HR technology, or a related field.

Experience working with Workday or another enterprise HRIS; direct Workday implementation experience is strongly preferred.

jobs.title: Hazardous Materials Handler
jobs.description:
Divergent is building the new industrial age. Every day, our teams design, manufacture, and assemble advanced systems for some of the world’s most demanding industries. Our integrated engineering and manufacturing platform transforms complex designs into production-ready solutions, helping customers move faster, build smarter, and deliver critical systems when they matter most. Divergent is a qualified Tier 1 supplier to global automotive OEMs and supports leading U.S. aerospace and defense companies.

Join us and help push the boundaries of what can be built.

Purpose

We are seeking a Hazardous Materials Handler to join our EHS team. This role will play a critical part in ensuring hazardous materials are handled and processed safely and with the highest level of environmental stewardship. The successful candidate will work closely with cross-functional teams to keep high-precision manufacturing processes running smoothly and safely. As a Hazardous Materials Handler you will be responsible for safe, compliant handling of regulated wastes as well as working throughout the business to ensure occupational safety and health requirements are met.

The Role

Regulated waste handling

Cradle-to-grave handling of regulated wastes in accordance with federal, state, and local requirements.

Occupational safety

Conduct occupational safety inspections and interventions utilizing safety inspection software in accordance with federal, state, and local requirements.

Industrial hygiene

Implement industrial hygiene requirements such as (but not limited to): chemical exposure identification/control, noise monitoring, and respiratory protection

Basic Qualifications

Ability to lawfully access information and technology that is subject to US export controls
At least 1 year of experience handling, packaging, and shipping regulated wastes.
Experience with chemical segregation including (but not limited to) flammables, corrosives, reactive materials.
Experience operating material handling equipment such as forklifts and pallet jacks.
Ability to wear personal protective equipment including (but not limited to) respiratory protection, flame-resistant uniform, and safety toe shoes.
Proven ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams, customers, and suppliers to ensure EHS requirements are met.
Clear communication and documentation skills to effectively log environmental compliance data, occupational safety inspections, and implemented corrective actions.
Working knowledge of regulations governing regulated waste such as (but not limited to): Resource Conservation & Recovery Act (RCRA 40 CFR).
General knowledge of occupational safety requirements (29 CFR 1910) such as (but not limited to): lockout/tagout, electrical safety, personal protective equipment, fall protection, and confined spaces.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in the additive manufacturing industry.
Current certifications for: RCRA (California and federal) and Department of Transportation (DOT)
Experience with Microsoft, Excel and general computer efficiency for documentation of records.

Work Environment

This role is based in a dynamic manufacturing environment with exposure to production areas, quality & material labs, and office settings.
Position requires frequent standing, walking, or lifting up to 50 pounds.
Mon-Fri (8am-5:30pm) Occasional coverage over 3-day weekends.
From time to time, you may be asked to work on special projects or to assist with other work. Your cooperation and assistance in performing such additional work is expected.

T03 / Hazardous Materials Handler III: $42.98 - $49.63

Pay Range: $35.16 USD - $49.63 USD

Holistic Compensation Package: Enjoy a world-class compensation package that includes a competitive salary, equity plan, and discretionary results-based incentive bonus opportunities, ensuring you're truly valued for your contributions.

Comprehensive Health and Wellness: Prioritize your well-being with our comprehensive health and wellness benefits, offering both HMO and Premium PPO options. Additionally, benefit from company-sponsored life insurance and short and long-term disability coverage for peace of mind.

* Performs other duties as assigned.

* Preferred: Degree, preferably in environmental studies/science, urban/environmental planning, biology, anthropology/archaeology, geography, engineering, or related field. Master's degree preferred.


**Experience**
* Required: 5 years of related experience.
* Preferred: Experience supporting environmental compliance and field implementation, including monitoring and permit tracking; assisting with scope review to identify regulations and permits; and supporting preparation and review of technical reports, permit applications, and environmental documents (e.g., CEQA, NEPA) is preferred.


**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**
* Required: Ability to independently manage moderately complex scientific workstreams.
* Required: Ability to influence project stakeholders through sound scientific reasoning.
* Required: Ability to resolve non\-routine technical issues using professional judgment.
* Required: Knowledge of integrated environmental systems and cause\-and\-effect relationships.
* Required: Knowledge of regulatory interpretation as it applies to specific environmental conditions.
* Required: Skill in analyzing environmental data and drawing defensible conclusions.
* Required: Skill in designing and executing defined environmental studies or monitoring efforts.
* Preferred: Knowledge of environmental compliance including field monitoring and permit condition tracking. Capable of working with diverse stakeholders. Familiarity with environmental regulations and review processes (e.g., CEQA, NEPA). Knowledge in one or more disciplines such as biological resources, air quality, or land use planning. Ability to perform regulatory research and project tasks.

jobs.title: Senior Technical Project Manager – Chlorinated Solvent Remediation
jobs.description:
Are you driven to grow, lead, and make a meaningful impact? At Apex, we're building more than a consulting and engineering firm—we're creating a place where your career accelerates, your contributions matter, and your potential is fully realized. We believe your growth is our growth, which is why we invest in your development at every stage of your career. Here, you'll work on projects that shape communities, protect the environment, and create lasting impact, all while being empowered with the autonomy and flexibility to do your best work.  

  

Fueled by high\-quality delivery, exceptional client retention, and strategic acquisitions, Apex Companies continues to rank among the fastest\-growing firms in the AEC industry, recently recognized by the Zweig Group for our industry\-leading growth. Our success is grounded in strong leadership, a collaborative culture, and a shared commitment to delivering exceptional outcomes.  

  

As we continue to expand, we're looking for high\-performing professionals who are ready to lead, collaborate, innovate, and create impact. At Apex, you help shape what's next. When we succeed together, we share in that success. All Apex positions are eligible for annual bonus opportunities, reinforcing our commitment to recognizing and rewarding meaningful contributions that drive our collective growth.

  

The Senior Technical Project Manager (PM) will lead and manage complex environmental investigation, remediation, and compliance projects involving chlorinated solvent impacts in soil, groundwater, sediment, soil vapor, and indoor air. The role requires strong technical leadership, client management, project delivery, staff development, and business development capabilities. Experience with large industrial, aerospace, manufacturing, military, and brownfield remediation programs is highly desirable. Based on current Stantec environmental PM roles, emphasis is placed on managing multidisciplinary teams, technical delivery, client relationships, and financial performance.


**Key Responsibilities**


**Project and Program Management**


* Manage large\-scale environmental remediation projects from proposal through closure.
* Develop project scopes, schedules, budgets, and health and safety plans.
* Lead multidisciplinary teams of geologists, engineers, hydrogeologists, risk assessors, and environmental scientists.
* Monitor project financial performance, including revenue, profitability, utilization, and forecasting.
* Coordinate subcontractors, laboratories, drilling contractors, and remediation vendors.
* Maintain quality assurance and quality control standards.


**Technical Leadership**


* Serve as a technical lead for sites impacted by:
	+ PCE (Tetrachloroethylene)
	+ TCE (Trichloroethylene)
	+ cis\-1,2\-DCE
	+ Vinyl Chloride
	+ Other chlorinated VOCs
* Design and oversee:
	+ Site investigations
	+ Groundwater characterization
	+ Soil vapor intrusion assessments
	+ Human health and ecological risk assessments
	+ Remedial investigations/feasibility studies (RI/FS)
	+ Corrective action programs
* Evaluate and implement remediation technologies such as:
	+ In situ chemical reduction (ISCR)
	+ In situ chemical oxidation (ISCO)
	+ Enhanced reductive dechlorination (ERD)
	+ Thermal remediation
	+ Soil vapor extraction (SVE)
	+ Dual\-phase extraction (DPE)
	+ Air sparging
	+ Monitored natural attenuation (MNA)

**Client Relationship Management**


* Act as primary client contact for key accounts.
* Support strategic planning with industrial, aerospace, petroleum, manufacturing, and government clients.
* Prepare and present technical findings to clients, regulators, and stakeholders.
* Maintain long\-term client relationships while identifying opportunities for additional services.


**Business Development**


* Lead proposal preparation and pricing.
* Support capture planning and opportunity pursuit.
* Identify new clients and expand existing accounts.
* Participate in industry organizations and conferences.


**Regulatory Expertise**



Demonstrated experience working with:


* EPA CERCLA/Superfund programs
* RCRA Corrective Action
* State cleanup programs
* Vapor intrusion guidance
* UST and industrial facility closure programs
* California DTSC and Regional Water Board programs (preferred for West Coast positions)


**Required Qualifications**


* S. or M.S. in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Geological Engineering, Hydrogeology, Geology, or related field.
* 12\+ years of environmental consulting experience.
* 7\+ years managing complex remediation projects.
* Demonstrated success managing projects exceeding $500K to $5M\+ annually.
* Significant chlorinated solvent investigation and remediation experience.


**Licenses and Certifications (Preferred)**


* California PE
* PG
* CHG
* PMP
* REM
* CHMM


**Success Factors**



The ideal candidate:


* Is recognized as a subject matter expert in chlorinated solvent remediation.
* Can mentor junior technical staff.
* Understands both technical and financial drivers of environmental consulting projects.
* Has strong client\-facing communication skills.
* Can grow strategic accounts while maintaining high\-quality project execution.


**Why you'll love working for us:**


* Company\-subsidized medical and dental.
* Company\-paid life, short, and long\-term disability.
* 401k match, tuition assistance, and more.
* Cross\-training and the ability to work on a variety of projects.
* Performance\-based bonuses or other incentives.
* Working with the best and brightest in the industry.
* 2,000\+ employee national firm with 70\+ locations across the US.

Position Title

Job Description

If this opportunity aligns with your strengths, background, and commitment to fostering inclusivity, we encourage you to apply! At the Oregon Health Authority (OHA), we value diversity and encourage applicants from all backgrounds and experiences to help us build a stronger, more equitable future for all.

Opportunity Awaits, Apply Today!
– Health Physicist- Licensing (Environmental Health Specialist 3)

The Oregon Health Authority (OHA), Public Health Division (PHD), Radiation Protection Services section is seeking a Health Physicist – Licensing (Environmental Health Specialist 3) to join its team.

In this role, the Health Physicist will provide guidance to public and private sector officials on radiation health and safety issues, drawing on environmental testing data and scientific research. This individual will interpret and explain applicable statutes, rules, policies, and procedures to licensees and applicants. They will also review radiation safety program requirements, identify areas within license applications that may require clarification or improvement, and offer appropriate recommendations. In addition, the position provides instruction to individuals or groups of licensees on the methods and procedures necessary to comply with regulatory standards.

For a full review of the position description, please
click here
.

These qualifications must be reflected in your application for consideration.

Two years of experience equivalent to an Environmental Health Specialist 2 working under general supervision of an environmental health specialist, conducting environmental health or hazardous materials investigations, inspecting facilities and equipment for environmental health regulation compliance, investigating and assessing the impact of adverse environmental conditions on the public health, preparing health permits, conducting studies and surveys, and developing solutions to environmental problems AND

A bachelor's degree with 45 quarter (30 semester) hours in a field of science.

Desired Attributes:
The following are desired attributes that we have identified as key to success for this role at OHA. These are the attributes we are looking for in our top candidate. If you possess any of these attributes, please highlight them in your application, resume, and address specifically in your cover letter.

Experience in advising public and private officials on radiation health and safety issues.
Experience in interpreting rules, policies, and procedures to radioactive material licensees.
Experience in reviewing the licensee’s radiation safety program and assessing needs for improvement.
Experience in providing methods and procedures for compliance with regulatory requirements.
Experience working with external partners, licensees and other local, state and federal agencies.
Ability to evaluate license applications and communicate with prospective licensees regarding missing information or clarification of supplied information.
Experience working with software such as Microsoft Office Suite, Word, Excel, Access and PowerPoint.

Preference Statement:

Supplemental Questions – Answer all supplemental questions completely and accurately.
Final Check! – Before submitting, confirm that all required materials are included, and your Workday Job History is current. The information in your application will be used to complete an Equal Pay Analysis to determine salary placement upon hire. Visit the Equal Pay Analysis Webpage for more information.

jobs.title: Air Quality Specialist
jobs.description:
Position Description

Purpose

The Air Quality Specialist / Engineer is responsible for preparing and submitting air quality permit applications for Teichert Materials stationary and portable equipment operations across California and western Nevada. The primary focus of this role is permitting: compiling emissions data for reporting, quantifying source emissions, preparing Authority to Construct (ATC) and Permit to Operate (PTO) applications, and managing them through district review to issuance.

This role serves as the company's technical resource for New Source Review, Best Available Control Technology (BACT) and toxics evaluations, CARB portable equipment (PERP) registration, and coordination with local air districts, the Nevada Division of Environmental Protection (NDEP), and Northern Nevada Public Health. The Air Quality Specialist / Engineer supports facility- and equipment-level compliance, tracks permit conditions and renewal deadlines, and drives regulatory readiness and risk mitigation across the Teichert Family of Companies.

Focus & Scope

Essential duties and responsibilities, i.e. those which are basic, necessary, and an integral part of the job, are indicated below:

Air Quality Permitting and Regulatory Analysis

Prepare, submit, and manage complete and technically defensible air quality permit applications for new, modified, relocated, stationary, and portable equipment and sources, including Authority to Construct (ATC), Permit to Operate (PTO), and applicable portable equipment registrations.
Quantify source-specific emissions, including NOx, SOx, CO, VOC, PM/PM10/PM2.5, and toxic air contaminants, using applicable regulatory methodologies, emission factors, and accepted calculation methods.
Evaluate projects, facilities, and equipment to determine applicable permitting requirements, including exemptions, New Source Review, Best Available Control Technology (BACT), offsets, air toxics requirements, and other federal, state, and local regulatory requirements.
Review draft permit conditions prior to ATC issuance, and negotiate practical, enforceable condition language with district permit engineers to minimize operational and compliance burden while meeting air quality standards.
Manage permit applications through agency review and issuance, including responding to completeness determinations, deficiency notices, and technical inquiries; evaluating proposed permit conditions; and working with regulatory agencies to establish practical and enforceable permit requirements.
Coordinate air quality permitting with California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review and other regulatory processes when applicable.

Regulatory Compliance and Reporting

Maintain and administer air quality permits, registrations, compliance obligations, and regulatory deadlines for Company operations, including permit and registration renewals, monitoring, recordkeeping, emissions inventories, testing, and reporting requirements.
Prepare and submit required air quality regulatory reports and inventories, including applicable criteria pollutant and toxic air contaminant reporting, CARB Criteria and Toxics Reporting (CTR), greenhouse gas reporting, and AB 2588 Air Toxics “Hot Spots” reporting.
Administer applicable AB 2588 requirements, including toxic air contaminant emissions inventories, prioritization and risk screening, and coordination of required health risk assessments, public notifications, or risk-reduction activities.
Coordinate and oversee source (stack) testing for stationary equipment — scheduling required tests with certified testing firms, preparing and submitting source test protocols for district approval, coordinating district witnessing, and reviewing test reports for compliance with permit conditions and applicable emission limits.
Monitor facility and equipment compliance with applicable permit conditions and regulatory requirements, including fuel usage, throughput, hours of operation, emission limits, monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting obligations; identify compliance risks and coordinate appropriate corrective actions.

Technical Evaluation and Field Support

Regularly access and evaluate active materials facilities, plants, equipment areas, and project sites to conduct source evaluations, obtain equipment and operational information, observe operating conditions, and support permitting and compliance activities (approximately 30% of work time, with the remaining time performing office-based permitting, analysis, and reporting functions). Site conditions may include uneven terrain, stairs or elevated areas, heavy moving equipment, dust, noise, and outdoor weather conditions.
Conduct or coordinate on-site evaluations of Company facilities, equipment, and project sites to identify applicable air quality permitting and compliance requirements and obtain technical and operational information necessary to support regulatory determinations, applications, and reporting.
Coordinate required source testing and other compliance evaluations, including test planning, regulatory agency coordination, review of technical results, and identification and resolution of potential compliance issues.
Provide technical guidance to operations, equipment, environmental, and project teams regarding air quality permitting and compliance requirements so regulatory considerations can be addressed during project planning, equipment acquisition or relocation, installation, and ongoing operations.

Agency and Organizational Representation

Serve as a Company technical representative and liaison with local Air Pollution Control Districts and Air Quality Management Districts, the California Air Resources Board (CARB), Nevada Division of Environmental Protection (NDEP), Northern Nevada Public Health (NNPH), consultants, testing firms, vendors, and other external parties regarding air quality permitting and compliance matters.
Support regulatory inspections, internal audits, enforcement matters, and corrective actions by evaluating compliance issues, assembling technical documentation, responding to regulatory inquiries, and developing or coordinating appropriate corrective action plans.
Represent the Company, as appropriate, in industry groups and regulatory proceedings; monitor emerging air quality laws and regulations; evaluate potential impacts to Company operations; and assist in developing comments or recommendations regarding proposed regulatory changes.

Compliance Systems and Risk Management

Develop and maintain accurate, organized, and audit-ready permitting and compliance records, calculation tools, application templates, tracking systems, procedures, and other documentation necessary to support regulatory compliance and continuity of operations.
Maintain expert and current knowledge of applicable federal, California, Nevada, and local air quality requirements and evaluate regulatory developments that may affect Company operations.
Provide management with timely information regarding pending permit applications, regulatory deadlines, deficiencies, emerging requirements, and compliance risks, including recommended actions, responsible parties, and appropriate timelines for resolution.
Develop and improve permitting, workflow, and compliance processes, tools, and documentation to promote consistency, regulatory readiness, operational efficiency, and sustainable compliance across Company operations.

Relationships, Qualifications & Requirements, And Competencies

Key Relationships

Reports To

Environmental Manager, Teichert Materials

Direct Reports

N/A

External Clients

Public agencies, federal, state, and local regulatory agencies, subcontractors, vendors, general public

Internal Clients

President of Teichert Materials; Director of Aggregate Resource Development (ARD) and Environmental Compliance; Teichert Materials Plant Managers, Superintendents, and Administrative Staff; Teichert Services Group; ARD; Data and Technology Services (DTS); and other business units

Education

Bachelor's degree in environmental engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, environmental science, or a related technical field preferred; equivalent combination of training, education, and experience will be considered.

Experience and Industry Expertise

Minimum of five (5) to eight (8) years of experience preparing air quality permit applications (Authority to Construct / Permit to Operate) for stationary or portable sources in California; experience with a California air district or as a permitting consultant preferred.
Working knowledge of the California local air district permitting system, New Source Review, BACT, air toxics evaluation, and CARB programs including PERP.
Experience with western Nevada air permitting (NDEP Bureau of Air Pollution Control and/or Northern Nevada Public Health) a plus.
Experience in the construction, aggregates, ready-mix, asphalt, or heavy equipment industries a plus.

Specific Job Requirements

Demonstrated ability to quantify source emissions using accepted emission factors and calculation methods, and to prepare complete, defensible permit applications.
Working understanding of how CEQA review interacts with air district permitting timelines.
Working knowledge of California AB 2588 (Air Toxics “Hot Spots”) requirements, including toxic emissions inventory, prioritization, and health risk assessment triggers.
Ability to interpret and apply federal, state, and local air quality regulations and to translate permit conditions into practical compliance requirements for field staff.
Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy; self-motivated with strong follow-through on applications and deadlines.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to negotiate permit conditions with district engineers and to explain requirements to non-technical staff in plain language.
Strong organizational and time-management skills; able to manage multiple concurrent applications and shifting district review timelines.
Strong project management skills with proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, especially Excel for emissions calculations, and the ability to quickly learn permitting and database tools.
Collaborative team player able to thrive in a matrixed management structure across multiple operating groups.
Commitment to workplace safety and support of corporate safety initiatives.
Willingness to adhere to the Company Code of Conduct consistently.
Some travel required to job sites and district offices in California and western Nevada.
Ability to travel regularly to Company facilities, project sites, regulatory agency offices, and other business locations throughout California and western Nevada.
A valid driver's license and acceptable driving record are required when operating a motor vehicle on Company business.
May require occasional work outside standard business hours, including early mornings, evenings, or weekends, to support regulatory deadlines, site activities, meetings, training, or time-sensitive operational matters.

Desirable Qualifications

Understanding of the working relationship between the CARB Portable Equipment Registration Program (PERP) and the Diesel Off-Road Online Reporting System (DOORS), including how portable and off-road diesel equipment is registered, reported, and kept compliant at both stationary facilities and temporary project sites.
Familiarity with distinguishing when equipment at a job site should be permitted by the local district, registered under PERP, or reported through DOORS, and how those pathways interact as equipment moves between sites.
Professional certification or coursework in air quality, environmental engineering, or a related field (e.g., QEP, CPEA, or equivalent).

Competencies

Building Relationships
Listening
Planning/Prioritizing
Initiative
Dependability
Judgement/Decision Making
Learning/Development
Managerial Courage
Safety

Equipment Used, Physical Demands, and Work Environment

**Find your further with Ventia as a Hydrographer / Environmental Scientist where your career takes you beyond the office and into some of Victoria and southern New South Wales most diverse and challenging environments. At Ventia no two days are the same.**

  

You will be at the forefront of environmental monitoring, working on critical water resource and environmental projects for major government, defence, and infrastructure clients. From conducting streamflow measurements during high\-flow events to deploying cutting edge monitoring technology in remote locations, you will play a key role in collecting the data that informs important environmental and water management decisions.

 **What’s on Offer**

* Attractive salary \& use of company vehicle for site visits
* Field work Monday to Thursday and catch up in the office with your team on Fridays
* Flexibility around start and finish times
* Career development, upskilling and training opportunities
* Small collaborative and supportive team
* Access to a variety of Health and Wellness initiatives \- including the EAP, Ventia's Healthy Minds program and Healthy Bodies program
* Employee benefits such as corporate travel discounts, Novated leases, private health discounts, credit discounts with retailers Australia wide including Woolworths, Coles, Booking.com and Expedia

 **About the Role**  

This hands\-on role combines fieldwork, advanced technology, data analysis, and problem solving, offering the opportunity to build expertise across a wide range of environmental disciplines. You will work with industry leading equipment including ADCPs, water quality skills in hydrography, environmental monitoring and data management.

  

Whether you are troubleshooting a monitoring station, surveying river cross\-sections, collecting groundwater samples, or analysing complex environmental datasets, you will be part of a team delivering meaningful outcomes for some of Australia’s most significant environmental projects.

  

Under the guidance of the Regional Manager, you will –

* Conduct field based environmental monitoring of surface and groundwater systems
* Collect, analyse, and report streamflow and water quality data
* Install and maintain hydrometric stations and instrumentation
* Perform site surveys, discharge measurements, and cross\-sectional profiling using ADV’s and ADCP’s
* Manage data using platform such HYDSTRA, ESDAT and Campbells
* Ensure compliance with OH\&S protocols and maintain high data quality standards
* Coordinate with laboratories and stakeholders throughout project lifecycles

 **Required Skills and Experience**

* Experienced in groundwater / surface water monitoring
* Enrolled in or completed a Diploma in Water Operations or Bachelor of Environmental Science (or similar)
* Proficient in Microsoft Excel and familiar with hydrological software
* Skilled in using SDI\-12 and 4\-20mA instrumentation
* A strong communicator with excellent time management and self\-motivation
* Willing to travel including overnight stays
* Certified in First Aid and CPR
* White / Red Card desirable
* Current drivers licence (4x4 driving certification and experience – desirable)

 **About Ventia**  

As a leading services provider, we maintain, operate, and manage the essential infrastructure that makes modern life possible across Australia and New Zealand. With more than 35,000 employees and subcontractors across 400 sites, joining Ventia means becoming part of a team that values its people, supports career growth, and helps everyone go further towards their full potential.  

  

Our commitment to Fairness, Inclusion and Respect shapes how we lead, collaborate, hire and support one another. We welcome applications from people of all ages, abilities and backgrounds, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, and people of all genders, identities, sexual orientations, beliefs and caring responsibilities. We are dedicated to providing an accessible recruitment process and encourage you to request adjustments at any stage.
